==English==

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|wandren}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wandrian|t=to wander, roam, fly around, hover; change; stray, err}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*wandarōn|t=to wander}}, from {{af|nocat=1|gmw-pro|*wandōn|t1=to turn, change|*-rōn|pos2=frequentative suffix}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|wander|t=to wander}}, {{cog|de|wandern|t=to wander, roam, hike, migrate}}, {{cog|nl|wandelen|t=to wander, roam, hike, migrate}}, {{cog|da|vandre|t=to wander, roam, hike, migrate}}, {{cog|sv|vandra|t=to wander, hike}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈwɒndə/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈwɑndɚ/|a=GA}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈwʊndə/<a:West Midlands,especially,Birmingham>|/ˈwʌndə/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-wander.ogg|a=GA}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɒndə(ɹ)|s=2}}
* {{hyph|en|wan|der}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To move without purpose or specified destination; often in search of [[livelihood]].
#: {{syn|en|err|roam}}
#: {{ux|en|to '''wander''' over the fields}}
#* {{RQ:KJV|Hebrews|11|37|passage=They '''wandered''' about in sheepskins and goatskins.}}
#* {{RQ:Chambers Younger Set|IX|passage=“A tight little craft,” was Austin’s invariable comment on the matron;{{nb...}}. ¶ Near her '''wandered''' her husband, orientally bland, invariably affable, and from time to time squinting sideways, as usual, in the ever-renewed expectation that he might catch a glimpse of his stiff, retroussé moustache.}}
#* {{RQ:Birmingham Gossamer|chapter=I|passage=There is an hour or two, after the passengers have embarked, which is disquieting and fussy.{{...}}Stewards, carrying cabin trunks, swarm in the corridors. Passengers '''wander''' restlessly about or hurry, with futile energy, from place to place.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[stray]]; stray from one's course; [[err]].
#: {{ux|en|A writer '''wanders''' from his subject.}}
#* {{RQ:KJV|Psalms|cxix|10|passage=O, let me not '''wander''' from thy commandments.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To commit [[adultery]].
#: {{syn|en|cheat}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To go somewhere indirectly or at varying speeds; to move in a curved path.
#: {{syn|en|drift}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} Of the mind, to lose focus or clarity of argument or attention.
#: {{syn|en|distract|scatter}}
